subject: Discovery recap: BrightCart embeddings/reranking (index scale, latency & cost targets)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightcart.com>, Priya Mehta <priyaa.mehta@brightcart.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: BrightCart embeddings/reranking (index scale, latency & cost targets)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of the discussion and the next steps we agreed on. Please flag anything I misunderstood.

High-level pain points you shared
- Search relevance on product search is inconsistent, especially for long-tail queries and phrase re-ordering. Merchandising rules are brittle.
- Current reranking pipeline is expensive and slow at scale (high per-query CPU cost when running ML rerankers).
- Batch indexing takes too long; you sometimes miss same-day inventory changes in recommendations.

Current stack / constraints you described
- Primary search: Elasticsearch + custom scoring, with a separate FAISS-based vector index for semantic results (hosted on a small on-prem cluster).
- Metadata and product store: Postgres; cache: Redis.
- Vector DB: in-house FAISS (CPU) for ~50M vectors (vector dim 1536).
- Embedding model today: an off-the-shelf embedding from a third-party API (pay-per-call).
- Query patterns: ~200 QPS peak on Black Friday-ish traffic; average day ~30–50 QPS. Most traffic is single-query low-latency (<100ms target) online lookups; offline batch jobs run nightly to reindex/refresh embeddings (batch of ~2–5M rows).

Success criteria (what good looks like)
- Reduce p95 end-to-end query latency for semantic + rerank from current ~220–300ms to sub-100ms (target p95 < 100ms; ideal < 50ms for critical flows).
- Reduce per-query inference cost for reranking by at least 40% versus current spend (targetized by batching/quantization/model selection).
- Keep index/search relevance metrics (NDCG@10) at or above current baseline while lowering cost.
- Pilot on a 5–10% slice of traffic for 4 weeks with clear evaluation metrics.

Technical constraints to consider
- On-prem FAISS is CPU-bound today; moving to GPU or a managed vector DB (Milvus/Pinecone/RedisVector) is on the table but needs cost/ops justification.
- Data residency: some product metadata must remain in your EU region for a subset of catalog—will need to confirm for pilot.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
1) I will share an architecture sketch and a one-pager with recommended approaches (GPU-hosted vector DB vs optimized CPU + quantized models) — attached. (Action: Marissa, by EOD tomorrow)
2) Alex/Priya to share a sample of the indexing job stats and a small eval dataset (we asked for a CSV with 5–10k query/ground-truth pairs). You mentioned you can provide that by early next week. (Action: BrightCart)
3) Schedule a 30-min tech sync with your infra/ops + our runtime engineer to validate network/latency constraints. Vivek suggested Wed or Thu next week. (Action: Marissa/Vivek)
4) We’ll propose a 4-week pilot plan and a cost estimate for running a 50M vector index on a GPU-optimized overlay + a low-cost quantized reranker.

Attachments included:
- brightcart-arch-20260210.png — proposed architecture sketch (PDF/PNG)
- brightcart-eval-sample.csv — sample eval CSV schema (example rows)

If that lines up, I’ll schedule the tech sync (Vivek will join) and draft the pilot plan.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 14:00 Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightcart.com> wrote:
> Hi Marissa — great call. A couple notes: we currently use a 1536-dim embedding and store ~50M vectors; peak query traffic roughly 200 QPS; these are the numbers we gave above.
>
> We can extract a 10k evaluation sample for you by Monday. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood supports partial on-prem indexing (i.e., keep metadata on-prem but host vectors in your cloud)?
>
> — Alex
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priyaa.mehta@brightcart.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: BrightCart embeddings/reranking (index scale, latency & cost targets)

Thanks Marissa — this looks accurate. A couple clarifying Qs: 
1) For the nightly batch, the job typically processes 3–4M changed rows (not always the full 5M). We can provide a job runtime profile.
2) For on-prem metadata: yes, product PII and certain regional pricing metadata must remain in our EU region; storing vectors in your cloud is fine as long as we have encryption-at-rest and a clear audit trail.

We’ll upload the 10k eval sample to the Drive link you provided by Mon morning. Happy to join the tech sync — Wed afternoon works best for our infra team.

Alex
Director, Search & Recommendations | BrightCart
alex.johnson@brightcart.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightcart.com>, Priya Mehta <priyaa.mehta@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: BrightCart embeddings/reranking (index scale, latency & cost targets)

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming the ask from our side for the tech sync:
- Provide a short (15–20 min) run-through of your current indexing pipeline and where FAISS runs (hosts, CPU/GPU profile).
- Share network topology / egress constraints for cloud-hosted vectors.
- Share the 10k eval + one representative heavy batch job profile.

After we get the eval and metrics I’ll run a lightweight perf/price estimation (GPU vs quantized CPU) and include a recommended pilot config. I’ll also include a minimal benchmark plan so we can measure p50/p95 latency and NDCG lift during the 4-week pilot.

I’ll propose Wed 2/18 2:00pm PT for the sync — Marissa will send the invite.

Cheers,
Vivek
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
